correctness.rationale: Pass for the repaired record (/workspace/repairs/2/RESULT.md and verify.py), which retains the gcd product and all density bounds. Writing Q_n=(α^n+β^n)/2, divisibility by an odd p is (α/β)^n=−1 in the cyclic norm-one subgroup (order p−(2/p)), including in the split algebra. There is a unique involution, so for even order h the indices are exactly odd multiples of e=h/2, with p∤e. Odd-exponent lifting for units α^e,β^e over the unramified p-adic component(s) gives ν_p(Q_em)=ν_p(Q_e)+ν_p(m) for odd m, enough for the whole p-part of n; p=2 never contributes. The obstruction p|gcd(n,Q_n) is an odd multiple of pe, whose intersections are empty in different 2-adic layers and are odd multiples of the lcm otherwise. With e≥log(2p−1)/log α, partial summation of Σ 1/(p log p) against π(x) bounded by 1.25506 x/log x gives exactly the stated tail. A finite interval n≤X incurs at most one rounding unit per prime ≤X, and π(X)/X→0; this justifies passage to natural density, not just convergence of formal inclusion–exclusion. The prime bound was independently certified through Dusart (6.6) for x≥60184 (log x>10, normalized factor ≤100/89), plus exact upward log-series comparisons at every prime 17≤p<60184 (tightest upper ratio at p=113, about 1.255058713). For the density endpoints, independent companion-matrix projective orders gave δ_59=154703748840589/176325122256360 and the ceiling sum 137404000609 across 6797 eligible primes of the 9591 odd primes ≤100000. Rational log bounds give tail ≤33236561673/662400500000<0.0502, implying the strict lower 0.812; δ≤δ_59<0.878. Direct integer recurrence confirmed 10000 gcds. Replay: python3 /workspace/reproductions/pell.py. The supplied verifier was inspected, not executed. Its original comment incorrectly bounded 1/log(100000)+1/(2 log²(100000)) by 0.0905 (instead about 0.0906311); its final floating comparison was numerically right but not an outward proof. The repaired copy uses exact rational inequalities and the independent test reproduced them. Neither finite check is a proof of the universal gcd rule or density existence.

value.rationale: Unlike qualitative density existence or known local lifting alone, the repaired result gives explicitly computable finite rational approximants and a guaranteed distance from the actual density. The 2-adic phase is arithmetically consequential, not an incidental filter, and the interval provides a quantitative benchmark for later refinements on indices of Lucas sequences of the second kind. The interval is not a precise decimal evaluation; neither the old two-prime rule nor a counterexample already known is relied on for the value assessment.
